extracted.intended_audience: voters, voting-rights advocates, ACLU supporters, policy and legal audiences
extracted.subtask_short: opposing EAC petition to require ID
extracted.subtask_description: Informational/advocacy page summarizing the ACLU's opposition to America First Legal's petition asking the Election Assistance Commission to amend the federal voter registration form to require documentary proof of U.S. citizenship. It outlines factual, legal, and equity arguments the ACLU submitted in public comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain NVRA one-page, streamlined federal voter registration form
rubrics_metrics.description: The federal voter registration form was created by the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA) and, as intended by the NVRA, the form is a one page, streamlined application that an individual can complete and mail-in without providing any additional documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not amend the federal form to add extra documentary requirements; the ACLU argues such changes would undermine the NVRA's purpose and could trigger widespread changes at the state level. Emphasize simplicity and mail-in accessibility when evaluating form changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not add a documentary proof-of-citizenship requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: AFL asks the EAC to require that any time an individual registers to vote or provides an update, they provide an actual copy of their passport or one of a few other limited U.S. citizenship documents with their registration form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat proposals to require passports or limited documents as unnecessary and likely harmful: the page labels this a 'show your papers' request and warns it would disenfranchise many eligible citizens. When evaluating such a proposal, weigh its necessity, proportionality, and likely real-world effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmation under penalty of perjury is sufficient for citizenship verification
rubrics_metrics.description: All registration forms for voting in federal elections, including the federal voter registration form, require voters to both check a box that they are a citizen of the U.S. and to sign under oath with a penalty of perjury that they are a U.S. citizen. When Congress enacted the NVRA in 1993, it determined that this positive affirmation along with significant penalties are sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the statutory framework and Congress's determination as a baseline standard: the existing check-box-plus-perjury mechanism is presented as an adequate verification mechanism that obviates the need for documentary proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing criminal prohibitions make additional documentary requirements unnecessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-U.S. citizens are prohibited by federal law from registering to vote or casting a ballot in federal elections; it's an existing crime punishable by up to five years in prison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider existing criminal penalties and enforcement mechanisms when assessing whether new documentary requirements are justified. The ACLU frames these penalties as part of the rationale for rejecting additional documentary burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate empirical evidence on the prevalence of non-citizen voting
rubrics_metrics.description: The current process has been working—the evidence is overwhelmingly clear that the instances of non-citizens voting are exceedingly rare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-makers should require persuasive empirical evidence of a widespread problem before adopting burdensome verification requirements. If data show rarity, the harms of a documentary requirement likely outweigh benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess risk of disenfranchisement and disparate impact
rubrics_metrics.description: If an additional documentary proof requirement is imposed, the impact on eligible U.S. citizens to register and vote would be significant. Tens of millions of citizens do not possess or have easy access to the documentation that would be required. There would be a highly discriminatory impact on naturalized citizens, voters with low incomes, voters of color, Native American voters, rural voters, and first-time voters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating rule changes, explicitly analyze who lacks access to required documents and the disproportionate burdens on protected or vulnerable groups. Equity and disparate-impact considerations should weigh heavily against proposals that would impede registration for those populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider state-level spillover effects of federal form changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the rules about the federal form are changed so that additional documentation is required, it is likely that many states would also change their own state voter registration forms to require documentary proof of citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess downstream effects: a federal change could cascade to state practices, magnifying national harms. Rulemaking should account for how states typically follow federal forms and the broader systemic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for relevant legal precedent and legislative context
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposal is similar to measures in President Trump's Executive Order 14,248 and the SAVE Act (H.R. 22) in Congress; the ACLU notes successful litigation stopping implementation of the EO (League of United Latin American Citizens v. Executive Office of the President, 780 F. Supp. 3d 135 (D.D.C. 2025)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking evaluations should take into account prior litigation outcomes, ongoing legislation, and the broader legal landscape. Use constitutional and statutory precedent to judge whether the proposed rule is lawful or likely to be overturned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningfully consider public comments and participation in rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The EAC asked for public comments by October 20, 2025; the ACLU and partners submitted robust comments in opposition, and approximately 383,153 comments were filed when the period closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should evaluate the substance, scale, and representativeness of public comments. High volumes of opposition and detailed submissions should factor into the agency's deliberations and record.
